 Iowa Senate race tightens with less than two weeks to election day 
 Polls show no clear front-runner between Hinson and Turek as spending nears record levels 
 Iowa’s Senate candidates are making their final pitch to voters with less than two weeks left before Election Day. By Andrew Pfeifer Published : Oct. 21, 2026 at 10:20 PM CDT | Updated : 46 minutes ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google DES MOINES, Iowa (WOWT) - Iowa’s Senate candidates are making their final pitch to voters with less than two weeks left before Election Day.
 A review of the top 12 preferred polls from The New York Times on the race shows no clear-cut leader. Seven of the 12 polls favor Republican Ashley Hinson, while five favor Democrat Josh Turek.
 Candidates campaign across the state
 Hinson campaigned in Glenwood on Wednesday with Sen. Joni Ernst, who is not seeking re-election. Turek held an event in Council Bluffs on Tuesday.
 Both candidates addressed prices, including health care costs.
 “There is more to do to lower prices. I think that there are a lot of Iowans who have been priced out of the American dream,” Hinson said.
 “I want to fight for affordable and accessible pharmaceuticals. I think it’s wrong to live in the richest country on Earth, and people can’t afford to take their medicine,” Turek said.
 Analyst points to competitive race
 Political analyst Dave Price said the tight race is surprising.
 “If you step back and maybe turn back the clock, you would think this is probably not going to be a super competitive race just because of what’s happened in the state over the past decade, where Republican candidates, frankly, have just done so much better,” Price said.
 Price said rising costs and the war with Iran are important issues to voters.
 “The war with Iran, inflation going up, people keep driving by gas stations and seeing how much more expensive it is. Their groceries are more expensive. All of those things, the cost of living, that all really kind of factor into the unpopularity of Donald Trump,” Price said.
 Spending expected to break records
 Price said spending in the race is on pace to be unprecedented.
 “That Senate race, that’s clearly going to be more money than we’ve ever seen spent on a United States Senate race in Iowa history. There is so much outside money, which just underscores how much each major political party wants to win this seat since it is an open seat,” Price said.
 Both campaigns are expected to continue crisscrossing the state through Election Day. Libertarian Thomas Lane is also on the ballot.
